No flat single-tone cel shading, photographic appearance, semi-realistic face or plastic 3D-render finish. Weather / season: a misty morning — soft fog outside.
Time of day: an overcast day — soft, shadowless grey-white light; soft even light, colours calm, no hard shadows.
Small moment: her breath fogs softly in the cold air.

POSTURE: standing.
COMPOSITION: a chest-up shot of her face, shoulders and expression; body turned three-quarters, her chest angled toward the right of the frame; head tilted slightly, her face turned a little toward the right of the frame; camera low, near the ground — level with her face when she sits, kneels or lies on the floor or a bed, looking up at her when she stands; her head and body angles are set by this line, not taken from the attached image.
Lens / perspective: 85mm-equivalent short-telephoto perspective from a suitable distance, with gentle background compression.
RIGHT HAND: her own right arm bends behind her head, the hand cradling the back of her head, her elbow raised beside her head.
LEFT HAND: her own left hand stays outside the frame.
GAZE: she looks up at the sky.
EXPRESSION: slightly furrowed brow, softened eyes, lips lightly pressed together.

Framing: a chest-up shot — the bottom edge crosses just below her bust; waist, hips and legs are out of frame.

Leave behind everything she wears in the attached image — no crown, tiara, helmet, feathers, headpiece, hairpins from it, armour or regalia; her hair is styled for the everyday outfit, with at most one small accessory.

Her element — fermium: element 100, the first to reach three digits, found together with her twin einsteinium in the fallout of the first hydrogen-bomb test in 1952, and named for the physicist who lit the first nuclear reactor, a pile of graphite blocks stacked in a squash court beneath the stands of a university sports field in the winter of 1942; she is the end of the road for building heavier elements by feeding neutrons to a reactor, because the next step splits apart almost at once, a wall no neutron can climb; her longest-lived form lasts only about a hundred days, and no one has ever gathered enough of her to see — may show in the outfit's details, motifs or small accessories.

Figure: keep her exact build from the attached image, neither slimmer nor fuller.

Light: the place's own light, lit and coloured the way this style renders light and skin.

One figure in focus, natural hands with five fingers, no text or numbers other than her element's own symbol and atomic number, no logo or watermark. No animals or other creatures.
